newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Royal & Sun in profit, sees savings.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Royal & Sun in profit, sees savings.

text.p: Newly-merged British insurer Royal & Sun Alliance (RSA) on Thursday reported a half-year profit that was ahead of market expectations and said it was on target to achieve full integration by 1998.
It confirmed that it expected to see a reduction of 175 million pounds ($274 million) in annual costs by then, and set out a timetable for how the integration process would proceed.
The merger of Royal and Sun in July created Britain's biggest insurer with a 5.4 billion pounds ($8.4 billion) market capitalisation.

Reporting pro-forma pre-tax operating profits of 450 million pounds ($703 million), down from 514 million ($803 million), last year but ahead of most analysts' forecasts, the group blamed the slide in profits on a 94 million pound ($147 million) increase in worldwide weather losses.
Total long-term business, meanwhile, rose by 12 percent.

Executive Deputy Chairman Roger Taylor said Royal & Sun had made rapid progress in integrating the two groups, commenting, "We shall be in a strong position to fulfil our potential as a leading insurance company in the U.K. and internationally."
Group Chief Executive Richard Gamble said the merger would result in more widely-spread profit sources, with the group less dependent on any one area of the world or any one product line.
